'''Robert Gravem Webb''' (February 18, 1927 – September 18, 2018<ref name=legacy>{{cite web |url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/elpasotimes/obituary.aspx?n=robert-gravem-webb-bob&pid=190336383&fhid=32251 |title=Dr. Robert "Bob" Gravem Webb  |author= |date=28 September 2018 |publisher=Legacy.com |accessdate=15 June 2019}}</ref>) was an [[Americans|American]] [[Herpetology|herpetologist]], expert in the [[systematics]] and [[biogeography]] of reptiles and amphibians, and professor emeritus of [[biological science]] at the [[University of Texas at El Paso]].<ref name="EDR"/>

Webb received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in zoology from the [[University of Kansas]] in 1960.<ref name="EDR">Beolens, Bo; Watkins, Michael; Grayson, Michael (2011). ''The Eponym Dictionary of Reptiles''. Baltimore: Johns Hopkins University Press. xiii + 296 pp. {{ISBN|978-1-4214-0135-5}}. ("Webb, R. G.", p. 280).</ref>

Webb had over a hundred publications to his name. He specialized in amphibians and reptiles of the southwestern [[United States]] and [[Mexico]].<ref name=legacy/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.utep.edu/leb/curators/webb.htm |title=Robert G. Webb |work=UTEP Biodiversity Collections Home Page |publisher=The University of Texas at El Paso |date=24 January 2011 |accessdate=4 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923004348/http://www.utep.edu/LEB/curators/webb.htm |archive-date=23 September 2015}}</ref>

The snake ''[[Lampropeltis webbi]]'' is named after him.<ref name="EDR"/><ref name=RDB>{{NRDB species|genus=Lampropeltis|species=webbi |accessdate=18 August 2015}}</ref>
